newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian investigators checking child molester plan.
newsitem.headline: Belgian investigators checking child molester plan.

text.p: Belgian investigators trying to find if a man accused of killing a young Moroccan girl five years ago was responsible for his actions are checking reports he questioned undertakers about corpse preservation techniques.

Patrick Derochette, a convicted child molester, was arrested in February after the discovery of the body of Loubna Benaissa stuffed into a steel trunk in the basement of a garage where he worked in the Ixelles suburb of Brussels.
"It was after the discovery of Loubna that my employees remembered the questions," local funeral director Paul Van Gossum said on Tuesday.
Eight-year-old Loubna disappeared in early August 1992 while out shopping for yoghurt for her mother.

There has been outrage in Belgium, already rocked to its roots by the discovery seven months earlier of four other young girls who died while in the hands of a paedophile gang, that police had failed for so long to find Loubna.

It was revealed that police had for days ignored the family's pleas to take the disappearance seriously, had given the garage only a cursory search in the early days despite Derochette's record and had then effectively closed the case.
Loubna's elder sister Nabela, now 18, and her father, a night time train cleaner, campaigned endlessly to keep the case alive, but ran into a brick wall of lethargy and anti-immigrant sentiment.
It was not until the discovery of the other four dead girls and the concentration of all missing children files in the hands of a new team of investigators that their pressure bore fruit.
Acting on information in the hands of the original investigators, police returned to the Ixelle's garage and finally found the little girl's body.
Derochette has been charged with abduction, illegal imprisonment and rape leading to the death of a child.
However, his lawyers have argued that his mind became unbalanced after he was raped by a judo instructor in his youth and that he was therefore not responsible for his actions.

The task of the investigators is to find whether Derochette posed his morbid questions before or after Loubna's disappearance -- in other words, whether his actions could be considered as premeditated.

Van Gossum said he could not recall whether the questions about embalming techniques had occurred before the disappearance, and he added that the investigators still had to talk to his employees about the matter.

To date police have made no direct connection between Derochette and convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux, who has been charged with the murder of the four other young Belgian girls whose bodies were discovered a year ago.

The crimes revolted Belgium, prompted speculation that Dutroux and possibly Derochette may have had friends in high places and catapulted the government into a series of reforms of the police and judicial systems.
They also revealed a trail of bungling, rivalry and incompetence among police and magistrates dealing with the original disappearances.
However, recent opinion polls have shown the public is discontent with the slow pace of the reforms and does not believe the full truth will ever be revealed.
